ARABIC LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #10
====

GRADE: Grade 6
SUBJECT: ARABIC LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening.

2. When practising Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation.

3. When practising Language Use, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Language Use.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Language Use.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language Use.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Language Use.

4. When practising Guided Reading: Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Guided Reading: Fluency.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Guided Reading: Fluency.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Guided Reading: Fluency.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Guided Reading: Fluency.

5. When practising Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation.

6. When practising Attentive Listening: Simple Instructions, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Attentive Listening: Simple Instructions.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Attentive Listening: Simple Instructions.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Attentive Listening: Simple Instructions.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive Listening: Simple Instructions.

7. When practising Conversational Skills, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Conversational Skills.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Conversational Skills.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Conversational Skills.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Conversational Skills.

8. In ARABIC LANGUAGE, the best classroom habit is: (1 mark)
   A. Avoid speaking to classmates
   B. Only memorise without using the language
   C. Practise listening, speaking, reading, and writing every day
   D. Mix random languages with no purpose

9. When practising Phonological Awareness: Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonological Awareness: Fluency.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Phonological Awareness: Fluency.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Phonological Awareness: Fluency.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Phonological Awareness: Fluency.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
10. In three clear sentences, explain Extensive Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

11. In three clear sentences, explain Reading for Comprehension and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

12. In three clear sentences, explain Extensive Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing: Sentences and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
